papers.title: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates.
papers.abstract: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction. Here, we present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that confines single cells in nanowells to obtain uniformly framed, r
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: The authors present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that uses nanowells to confine single cells in uniform positions, improving morphological profiling for mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis in drug discovery. This approach addresses limitations of conventional workflows, such as unreliable cell segmentation and reliance on hand-engineered features, by leveraging deep learning for more robust single-cell phenotyping.

papers.title: Synthesis and antiproliferative screening of para-halogenated 4H-chromene-benzene hybrids: crystallographic, and molecular-docking studies.
papers.abstract: A series of novel 4H-chromene-benzene hybrids bearing para-halogen substituents (F, Cl, Br, I) on the phenyl moiety were efficiently synthesized via an ultrasonic-assisted one-pot three-component cyclocondensation reaction. The reaction proceeded in 93-96% yield within 2 minutes under mild conditions. The structures were fully characterized by IR, 1D/2D NMR, mass spectrometry, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction of 4b. The antiproliferative activity of all compounds was evaluated against twelve human cancer cell lines using the MTT assay. Compound 4b (4-Cl) exhibited the most broadly active p
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of 4H-chromene-benzene hybrids with para-halogen substituents using a fast ultrasonic-assisted one-pot reaction (93-96% yield in 2 minutes) and characterized them by NMR, mass spectrometry, and X-ray crystallography. They screened all compounds against twelve human cancer cell lines and found that the 4-chloro derivative (4b) showed the broadest antiproliferative activity, supported by molecular docking studies. This is a medicinal chemistry structure-activity study identifying a lead scaffold for further anticancer development.

papers.title: Surrogate Machine Learning Models for ADME Prediction: From Synthetic Labels to Experimental Data.
papers.abstract: Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental data sets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate data sets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper examines surrogate machine learning models for predicting ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) properties in drug discovery, where experimental data are scarce. It investigates using synthetic labels—predictions from models trained on experimental data—as a data augmentation or sharing strategy, and compares how models trained on synthetic versus experimental labels perform and generalize. The work highlights that training data composition critically affects ADME model performance and generalizability.

papers.title: AI-Driven Discovery of Nodakenin as a Novel Molecular Glue Targeting the TRIM28-NR4A1-LCN2 Axis to Induce Ferroptosis in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma remains a malignancy requiring novel interventions. While triggering ferroptosis has emerged as a promising anti-tumor strategy, the targetable molecular vulnerabilities governing this process remain incompletely understood. Here, through artificial intelligence (AI)-driven virtual screening, we identified the coumarin derivative Nodakenin (NK) as a potent inhibitor of nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1), an orphan nuclear receptor highly expressed in malignant melanoma cells. Transcriptomic, biochemical, and structural analyses revealed that NK triggers ferroptosis
papers.summary: Using AI-driven virtual screening, the authors identified the coumarin derivative Nodakenin as an inhibitor of the orphan nuclear receptor NR4A1, which is highly expressed in melanoma cells. Biochemical and structural analyses indicate that Nodakenin acts as a molecular glue bridging TRIM28 and NR4A1, disrupting the TRIM28-NR4A1-LCN2 axis and thereby inducing ferroptosis in melanoma. This work nominates a new compound and a targetable axis for melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs). Despite rapid advances in PROTAC development, successful translation depends on interconnected determinants, including target degradability, ubiquitin ligase (E3) recruitment,
papers.summary: This review examines targeted protein degradation as a therapeutic strategy, focusing on PROTACs that hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate disease-causing proteins rather than merely inhibiting them. It discusses key determinants of successful PROTAC translation—target degradability, E3 ligase selection, and linker design—and highlights how AI-driven approaches are being integrated into the design pipeline. The paper frames TPD as an emerging paradigm that expands the druggable proteome beyond conventional inhibitor-based targets.

papers.title: canSAR 2026-an update to the public drug discovery knowledgebase.
papers.abstract: canSAR (https://cansar.ai) serves as the world's largest public platform for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It serves as an exploration and hypothesis generation platform for drug discovery through (i) fully integrating large, multidisciplinary data from public resources, as well as bespoke curated data, creating a connected, navigable drug discovery knowledge map; and (ii) applying a suite of machine learning and AI tools to generate novel insights. We share the latest updates to canSAR highlighting growth across all data, enhancements to the predictive algorithms, and cont
papers.summary: canSAR 2026 is an updated public knowledgebase for cancer drug discovery that integrates large multidisciplinary datasets into a connected knowledge map and applies machine learning and AI tools to generate new insights. The update highlights growth across all data types, improvements to predictive algorithms, and continued expansion of the platform's capabilities.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Elbasvir as a Theoretical Candidate for PFOS-Associated Gut and Skin Shared Pathologies.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently co-occur along the gut-skin axis, yet the systemic triggers, particularly environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals like perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to propose a computational framework for the shared molecular signatures of PFOS-driven AD and IBD comorbidity. Utilizing large-scale clinical transcriptomic cohorts and machine learning, we computationally predicted the transcription factor MYC as a potential core pathologic
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to identify shared molecular signatures linking PFOS exposure to co-occurring atopic dermatitis and inflammatory bowel disease along the gut-skin axis. Machine learning on clinical transcriptomic cohorts predicted MYC as a core transcription factor, and the authors computationally nominate the drug elbasvir as a theoretical candidate for these PFOS-associated pathologies. All findings are computational predictions without experimental validation.

papers.title: DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.
papers.abstract: The Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb; https://dgidb.org) is an open-access aggregate knowledgebase that normalizes and centralizes drug-gene interaction and gene annotation data from diverse therapeutic and biomedical sources. Since its previous update, DGIdb has expanded its data content and added new tooling to better support programmatic access and local deployment. This release updates existing sources and incorporates three new sources of interaction data, including annotation data from the Molecular Oncology Almanac, the PRISM Repurposing Dataset, and the Broad Institute Drug Repurp
papers.summary: DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access knowledgebase that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new interaction datasets (Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing, and Broad Institute Drug Repurposing). The release also improves programmatic access and local deployment options, making it easier for researchers to integrate druggable-genome data into their own pipelines.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies. Deep-learning imaging syste
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys the use of machine learning and deep learning across cardiovascular research, covering imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. It emphasizes distinguishing genuine AI contributions from routine bioinformatics and biophysical modeling, and evaluates studies based on independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference. The review provides a critical framework for assessing AI applications in basic and translational cardiovascular science.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components and trigger inflammatory signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic immunopathology. It combines cheminformatics and machine-learning approaches to identify potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. The work is a broad synthesis aimed at guiding drug discovery for Mycoplasma-associated inflammatory disease.

papers.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that combining single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is enabling 'virtual cell' models and digital twins that capture cellular dynamics, spatial context, and treatment responses rather than static molecular snapshots. The authors frame agentic AI as a driver of this shift and discuss its implications for multi-omics integration and drug discovery. It is a conceptual/opinion piece rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: From static structures to conformational ensembles: Artificial intelligence for protein sampling and dynamics.
papers.abstract: After sparking a revolution in protein structure prediction, machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) are now reshaping the modeling of protein conformational ensembles and dynamics. A fast, scalable, and accurate representation of protein conformational ensembles could enable genome-scale studies of protein function, with broad applications in drug discovery and protein engineering. The challenges associated with this goal, however, are far greater than those involved in single structure prediction because of the broad timescales spanned by protein motion, the complex relations
papers.summary: This review discusses how machine learning and AI are moving beyond static protein structure prediction to modeling protein conformational ensembles and dynamics. It highlights the challenges posed by the broad timescales of protein motion and the complex relationships involved, while noting potential applications in drug discovery and protein engineering.

papers.title: Benchmarking Structural Models of α-Conotoxin-Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor Complexes: Apo-Conformer Selection, Interface Information, and Deep-Learning Co-Folding.
papers.abstract: Conopeptides are a proven drug source, but translation stalls at one step: predicting how a peptide engages a human receptor before a clinical program commits. We benchmarked modelling of α-conotoxin-nicotinic acetylcholine receptor complexes at two deposited structures, kept separate because their data-leakage status differs: a human α7-ImI cryo-EM complex, rated MEDIUM leakage risk, and a non-human Aplysia acetylcholine-binding protein-RgIA crystal that lies inside the Boltz-2 training window and is therefore a positive control, not a held-out test. Apo-conformer choice fixes attainable accu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational methods for predicting how α-conotoxin peptides bind to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, a key step in peptide drug development. The authors compare approaches including apo-conformer selection and deep-learning co-folding against two experimental structures, finding that the choice of starting receptor conformation strongly constrains achievable accuracy. They also flag data-leakage concerns, noting that one test structure falls within the Boltz-2 training window and thus serves only as a positive control rather than a true held-out benchmark.

papers.title: Machine learning for small-molecule antibiotics - discovery to pre-clinical optimization.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health crisis, with 4.71 million associated deaths and 1.14 million attributable deaths in 2021. By 2050, these tolls are forecasted to rise to 8.22 million associated deaths and 1.91 million attributable deaths annually. Despite this growing burden, the antibacterial pipeline is alarmingly lean, with few candidates exhibiting truly novel mechanisms of action (MOA). This innovation gap is worsened by the lack of economic incentives for large pharmaceutical companies to develop new antibiotics, placing increasing pressure
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning is being applied across the antibiotic discovery pipeline, from initial compound screening through pre-clinical optimization, in response to the escalating antimicrobial resistance crisis. It highlights the urgent need for novel antibiotics given the sparse pipeline and frames ML as a tool to accelerate discovery despite weak economic incentives for traditional drug development.

papers.title: Advancing the Alzheimer's disease research and care pipeline with agentic artificial intelligence: Opportunities, challenges, and priorities from the international clinical trials on Alzheimer's disease (CTAD) task force.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds unprecedented potential to transform the entire Alzheimer's Disease and related dementias (ADRD) research and care continuum. During the 2025 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference, the CTAD Task Force reviewed recent advances in the field, highlighting the emerging role of agentic AI, and discussed priorities to guide future AI-driven innovation in ADRD. Agentic AI co-scientists are emerging as transformative tools to accelerate scientific discovery by autonomously integrating multimodal data, generating and evaluating new hypotheses, and c
papers.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
papers.summary: This task force perspective from the CTAD conference reviews how agentic AI—systems that can autonomously integrate multimodal data and generate and evaluate hypotheses—could accelerate Alzheimer's disease and related dementias research and care. It outlines opportunities and challenges and proposes priorities to guide future AI-driven innovation across the ADRD research and care continuum.

papers.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
papers.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This review integrates traditional disease classification systems with modern computational approaches for herbal drug discovery, arguing that in-silico ethnopharmacology can help identify bioactive phytochemicals and their mechanisms of action. It surveys how structural diversity and favorable safety profiles of herbal compounds make them attractive drug candidates, while emphasizing the need for rigorous mechanistic investigation to enable clinical translation.

papers.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline.
papers.summary: BioLM-Score introduces a protein-ligand scoring method that conditions geometric potentials on pretrained biomolecular language model representations, aiming to improve affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening simultaneously. The authors test whether such language priors enhance scoring performance under a controlled geometric baseline, addressing the generalization limits of purely geometric likelihood models when structural training coverage is sparse.

papers.title: A Machine Learning-Enhanced Ligand-Based Workflow Identifies Novel Cryptosporidium parvum Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Cryptosporidium parasites are a leading cause of waterborne disease worldwide, causing life-threatening diarrhea and malnutrition in young children and people with HIV. Currently, nitazoxanide is the only FDA-approved treatment, but it is largely ineffective in severely immunocompromised patients, highlighting the need for new therapies. Here, we use a ligand-based virtual screening workflow that integrates Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to screen a subset of Enamine's REAL database comprising 51 million virtual compounds. Across two screening campa
papers.summary: The authors developed a ligand-based virtual screening workflow combining Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to search 51 million virtual compounds from Enamine's REAL database for new Cryptosporidium parvum inhibitors. This approach identified novel candidate compounds targeting a parasite that causes life-threatening diarrhea, for which only one largely ineffective FDA-approved drug exists.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing in Pre-Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design.
papers.abstract: Pre-eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy affecting 3-8% of pregnancies worldwide, with no disease-modifying therapy currently available. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy, yet no candidate has been validated to date. Pregnancy-associated physiological changes alter drug pharmacokinetics (PK), and pre-eclampsia itself may further modify drug disposition, complicating dose selection and contributing to inconclusive clinical trial outcomes. A structured literature search identified six prospective or randomized controlled trials of repurposed drugs for established pre-ecla
papers.summary: This review examines why drug repurposing trials for pre-eclampsia have so far failed to identify a disease-modifying therapy, focusing on how pregnancy-related physiological changes and pre-eclampsia itself alter drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Based on a structured search of six prospective or randomized controlled trials, the authors argue that inadequate attention to maternal PK/PD in trial design contributes to inconclusive results and propose PK/PD-informed approaches for future trials.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint benchmarks protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction methods on their ability to predict mutation-dependent drug responses, using deep mutational scanning data for the MET kinase across 11 inhibitor conditions. The authors find that these models often fail to generalize beyond their training sets, particularly when small mutations cause large shifts in drug sensitivity. The work highlights a key limitation of current computational drug discovery approaches and provides a systematic evaluation framework for future model development.

papers.title: Who Knows Medicinal Chemistry? Expertise, Attrition, and the Dissolving Boundaries of a Craft.
papers.abstract: Medicinal chemistry treats expertise as something one possesses or lacks, and arranges people accordingly. Yet the knowledge is largely tacit, its outcomes are dominated by attrition, and its boundaries are dissolving as new modalities, AI, and cross-organizational work draw other disciplines into design. This Viewpoint offers a more defensible measure of expertise.
papers.summary: This Viewpoint argues that medicinal chemistry expertise is largely tacit and poorly captured by binary possess-or-lack classifications, especially given high attrition in drug discovery and the field's dissolving boundaries as AI, new modalities, and cross-disciplinary teams enter molecular design. The author proposes a more defensible way to measure expertise that better reflects these realities.

papers.title: A Hybrid Ligand- and Structure-Based Drug Design Invoked through Square Attention in Protein-Ligand Transformer.
papers.abstract: Computer-aided molecular design based on evaluation of protein-ligand (PL) binding affinity is important for accelerating drug discovery. A deep-learning model for natural language processing (NLP) involving an attention mechanism (i.e., Transformer) is expected to improve the PL-affinity evaluation along with clarifying amino acid residues and ligand atoms that are responsible for molecular interactions. However, the original attention (i.e., a scaled dot-product with row-wise Softmax normalization) is an adapted method for relationships between homogeneous inputs (e.g., two sentences in the
papers.summary: The paper introduces a Transformer-based deep learning model that uses a novel 'square attention' mechanism to jointly evaluate protein-ligand binding affinity while also identifying the specific amino acid residues and ligand atoms driving the interaction. This hybrid ligand- and structure-based approach aims to improve computer-aided drug design by making affinity predictions more interpretable.

papers.title: Phenylpropanoid Amides from Buteae monospermae Semen as Hepcidin-Modulating Candidates for Anemia of Inflammation: Network Pharmacology, Deep Learning Prediction, and In Vitro Validation.
papers.abstract: Anemia of inflammation (AI) is largely driven by interleukin-6 (IL-6)-induced hepcidin overproduction, which disrupts systemic iron homeostasis. Buteae monospermae Semen (BMS), the seeds of Butea monosperma (Lam.) Kuntze and a traditional Tibetan medicine, has long been used for blood-related disorders, yet its active constituents against AI remain unclear. Here, an integrated strategy combining ADMET screening, network pharmacology, deep learning-based affinity prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro validation was applied to 58 BMS-derived compounds. Forty-
papers.summary: This study identifies phenylpropanoid amides from Butea monosperma seeds as potential modulators of hepcidin, the hormone that drives anemia of inflammation by disrupting iron homeostasis. Using a pipeline of ADMET screening, network pharmacology, deep learning-based affinity prediction, docking, and molecular dynamics, followed by in vitro validation, the authors screened 58 compounds and narrowed them to a set of candidates. The work provides a computational-to-experimental framework for discovering natural-product leads against IL-6-driven hepcidin overproduction.

papers.title: GAC-BiT-CNN: A Hybrid Generative Adversarial Capsule-Transformer-CNN Model with Fused Protein Language Model Embeddings for Methyltransferase Prediction.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferases (MTs) are a functionally diverse class of enzymes that catalyse methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to DNA, RNA, and proteins, thereby regulating epigenetic programming, gene expression, and numerous disease processes. Dysregulation of these enzymes is implicated in a wide spectrum of human cancers and neurodegenerative disorders, making their accurate computational identification a priority in both basic research and drug discovery. We present GAC-BiT-CNN, a novel hybrid deep learning framework integrating Generative Adversarial Capsule Networks (GAC),
papers.summary: The authors present GAC-BiT-CNN, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines generative adversarial capsule networks, a bidirectional transformer, and a convolutional neural network, using fused protein language model embeddings to predict methyltransferases. The model is positioned as a computational tool for identifying these epigenetically important enzymes, which are implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative disease. The abstract is truncated, so reported performance and validation results are not available.

papers.title: Integrated Biochemical and Computational Evaluation of Bis-Imidazolium Derivatives 3e-3g in Cholinesterase and HIV-1 Reverse Transcriptase Assays.
papers.abstract: Bis-imidazolium derivatives (3e, 3f, 3g) were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE), butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), and human immunodeficiency virus type 1 reverse transcriptase (HIV-1 RT) using colorimetric assays and molecular docking. For the HIV-1 RT-3e complex, a 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area (MM/GBSA) analysis were performed. Compound 3e emerged as the most active derivative, showing the lowest half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values: 13.36 µg/mL for AChE, 4.95 µg/mL for BCh
papers.summary: The study evaluates three bis-imidazolium derivatives (3e, 3f, 3g) for inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, and HIV-1 reverse transcriptase using colorimetric assays and molecular docking. Compound 3e showed the strongest activity, with IC50 values of 13.36 µg/mL for AChE and 4.95 µg/mL for BChE, and its complex with HIV-1 RT was further analyzed by 100 ns MD simulation and MM/GBSA. The work is an early-stage in vitro and computational characterization of these compounds as dual-target cholinesterase/HIV-RT inhibitors.

papers.title: A TLR4-Associated Microglia-Endothelial Inflammatory Axis in Drug-Resistant Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: Integrated Transcriptomic and Genetic Evidence.
papers.abstract: Microglia-driven neuroinflammation contributes to epileptogenesis and drug resistance in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), but the cellular organization of the neuroinflammatory hub and its coupling to the cerebrovascular endothelium remain unresolved. We performed a retrospective secondary analysis of publicly available datasets, integrating paired hippocampal bulk transcriptomics (GSE134697), an integrated temporal-lobe single-cell/nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) atlas (9 patients with drug-resistant TLE and 4 controls), two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and summary-based Mendelian r
papers.summary: This study integrates public hippocampal bulk transcriptomics, a single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq atlas of drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, and Mendelian randomization to identify a TLR4-associated inflammatory axis linking microglia to cerebrovascular endothelial cells. The findings suggest that microglia-endothelial crosstalk via TLR4 signaling contributes to neuroinflammation and drug resistance in TLE, supported by both transcriptomic and genetic evidence.

papers.title: How Reliable Is In Silico ADMET Profiling? A Comparison of Tools Complementing Experimental In Vitro Analyses of Newly Developed Breast Cancer Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: In silico analyses, including absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) profiling and drug-likeness evaluations, constitute powerful tools in modern drug discovery. These computational methods enable high-throughput screening of molecular libraries to assess therapeutic potential while identifying unfavourable pharmacokinetic and toxicological profiles early in the development process. To bridge the gap between computational models and empirical data, this study evaluates the reliability and limitations of predictive ADMET profiling by comparing in silico outputs ac
papers.summary: This study benchmarks several in silico ADMET prediction tools against experimental in vitro data for newly developed breast cancer therapeutics, assessing how well computational predictions match empirical measurements. The authors identify where computational models agree with or diverge from experimental results, highlighting both the utility and limitations of ADMET profiling in early drug discovery. The work provides practical guidance on the reliability of these tools for prioritizing candidate compounds.

papers.title: Prediction of Molecular Physicochemical Properties Using Molecular Structure and Characteristics.
papers.abstract: The prediction of molecular physicochemical properties-such as solubility, hydration free energy, and lipophilicity-plays a crucial role in multiple fields, including drug discovery and materials science. Current prediction methods predominantly fall into two categories: machine learning methods based on molecular descriptors and deep learning methods that learn representations directly from molecular structures. However, when evaluated under rigorous scaffold splitting, these methods often exhibit limited generalization capability, resulting in unsatisfactory prediction accuracy. In this stud
papers.summary: This study addresses the limited generalization of current molecular property prediction methods under rigorous scaffold splitting by proposing an approach that combines molecular structure with additional characteristics. The work aims to improve prediction accuracy for properties like solubility, hydration free energy, and lipophilicity, which are critical in drug discovery and materials science. The abstract is truncated, so the specific method and quantitative results are not fully described.

papers.title: Characterization and Evaluation of the Neuroprotective Potential of Peptides Derived from Holothuria scabra Inner Wall Proteins: An In Vitro Study.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction driven by interconnected mechanisms, including oxidative stress, apoptosis, and impaired protein homeostasis. Marine-derived proteins and peptides represent promising sources of multifunctional neuroprotective agents; however, the neuroprotective potential of gastrointestinal digestion-derived peptides from Holothuria scabra remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of a gastrointestinal digest of H. scabra inner-wall proteins (IWD), a mixture of digestion-derived peptides,
papers.summary: This study characterizes peptides generated by simulated gastrointestinal digestion of inner-wall proteins from the sea cucumber Holothuria scabra and tests their neuroprotective activity in vitro. The digest mixture showed protective effects against oxidative stress, apoptosis, and protein-homeostasis disruption in neuronal models, suggesting marine-derived peptides as candidate multifunctional neuroprotective agents. The work is preliminary and limited to cell-based assays.

papers.title: From Computational Prioritization to Material Supply: A Proposed Two-Axis Record for Marine Invertebrate-Associated Natural Products and Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Marine natural products can show biological activity while remaining difficult to identify, reproduce, or obtain in sufficient quantity. This critical narrative review examines that mismatch and proposes a linked record for each exact chemical entity-indication pair. The documented evaluation stage (E1-E4) records computational, in vitro, animal, or human evaluation; the production/access stage (S1-S5) records physical access, an executed laboratory route, controlled pilot production, good manufacturing practice (GMP) clinical manufacture, or established commercial manufacture. Neither coordin
papers.summary: This critical review proposes a two-axis record for marine invertebrate-derived natural products that links each chemical entity–indication pair to both its evaluation stage (E1–E4, from computational to human) and its production/access stage (S1–S5, from physical access to commercial manufacture). The framework aims to expose the common mismatch between biological promise and the ability to identify, reproduce, or supply compounds in sufficient quantity, making such gaps explicit rather than implicit.

papers.title: Fast, lightweight BBB permeability predictions for molecular design.
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a selectively permeable border that regulates the transport of chemical compounds into and out of the central nervous system (CNS). To discover medicinal drugs that can target the CNS, we must be able to efficiently screen pools of potential candidate CNS-targeting drugs to identify those that can permeate the BBB. However, drugs that readily permeate the BBB are comparatively rare, thus CNS drug discovery typically requires screening very large candidate libraries. In the last two decades, a diverse portfolio of machine learning models has been developed to pr
papers.summary: This paper presents a fast, lightweight machine learning approach for predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, addressing the need to efficiently screen large candidate libraries in CNS drug discovery. Since BBB-permeable compounds are rare, such predictive models help prioritize candidates before costly experimental testing. The work contributes a practical computational tool for molecular design pipelines targeting central nervous system therapeutics.

papers.title: A trustworthy semantic knowledge network linking data-driven cell phenotypes to diseases and drugs.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association and other genetic studies have identified genes involved in disease pathogenesis, and their encoded proteins have provided therapeutic targets. However, little is known about which cells are the functional home of these disease-associated genes and proteins. Single-cell technologies are enabling high-resolution profiling of cell phenotypes and revealing cellular contexts of disease, yet much of the resulting knowledge remains embedded in individual datasets and scientific literature. To address these gaps, the National Library of Medicine has developed Cell Knowledge Ne
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The National Library of Medicine has developed Cell Knowledge Network, a semantic knowledge graph that integrates single-cell data-driven cell phenotypes with disease and drug information. This resource aims to connect disease-associated genes and proteins to the specific cell types where they function, addressing the gap between genetic findings and cellular context. The network is designed to be trustworthy and linkable, enabling researchers to query cell phenotypes in relation to diseases and therapeutics.

papers.title: Atractylenolide II Alleviates 5-Fluorouracil-Induced Intestinal Toxicity Through Potentially Targeting the TLR4-Mediated MYD88/NF-κB Signaling Pathway: An Integrated In Silico and In Vitro Study.
papers.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a potent compound in anti-tumor chemotherapy; however, its clinical utility is hampered by dose-limiting intestinal toxicity. Atractylenolide II (AT-II), a bioactive sesquiterpene derived from Atractylodis Rhizoma, has reported anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective activities. In this study, we employed an integrated strategy combining chemical characterization, computational pharmacology, and in vitro experiments to investigate the protective effect of AT-II against 5-FU-induced intestinal toxicity and clarify its potential target-associated mechanism. UHPLC-QE-MS was
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Atractylenolide II (AT-II), a plant-derived compound, can protect intestinal cells from the toxic side effects of the chemotherapy drug 5-fluorouracil. Using computational modeling and cell-based experiments, the authors propose that AT-II works by targeting TLR4 and dampening the MYD88/NF-κB inflammatory signaling pathway. The findings suggest a potential natural adjunct to reduce chemotherapy-induced gut damage, though validation in animal models or clinical settings is still needed.

papers.title: Biological and In Silico Evaluation of Two Nitrogen-Sulfur Heterocycles: Limited Cytotoxic, Antioxidant, and Antimicrobial Activities With Preliminary Anti-Inflammatory Effects.
papers.abstract: In this study, two nitrogen-sulfur-containing heterocyclic compounds, 9 and 10, were synthesized, and their biological activities were evaluated together with in silico prediction of selected ADME/T properties. Their cytotoxic effects were tested across multiple cancer cell lines and a noncancerous cell line, while antimicrobial activity was evaluated against bacterial and fungal strains. Antioxidant capacity was investigated using FRAP, DPPH, ABTS, and phosphomolybdenum assays. Preliminary anti-inflammatory effects were evaluated by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production and the expression of
papers.summary: Two new nitrogen-sulfur heterocyclic compounds were synthesized and tested across cancer cell lines, microbial strains, and antioxidant assays, with in silico ADME/T predictions and preliminary anti-inflammatory evaluation via nitric oxide production. The compounds showed limited cytotoxic, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activity, with only preliminary anti-inflammatory effects observed. Overall the biological profile is modest, and the work is primarily a synthetic and screening report rather than a discovery of potent bioactivity.

papers.title: Novel Thiochroman-4-one Derivatives Bearing a Thiosemicarbazide Scaffold With Potential Antioxidant, α-Glucosidase Inhibitory, and Antibacterial Activities.
papers.abstract: In this work, a series of novel thiochroman-4-one derivatives incorporating a thiosemicarbazide moiety were rationally designed and synthesized. In vitro bioactivity assays demonstrated that most target compounds exerted potent ABTS radical scavenging and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities. Notably, compound 6m exhibited superior bioactivities, with an IC50 value of 12.96 µM for ABTS radical scavenging and 27.48 µM for α-glucosidase inhibition, which were markedly stronger than those of the positive controls Trolox and acarbose, respectively. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics (M
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of a series of thiochroman-4-one derivatives containing a thiosemicarbazide moiety, with the goal of finding compounds that act as antioxidants, α-glucosidase inhibitors, and antibacterials. In vitro assays showed that most compounds had potent ABTS radical scavenging and α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, with compound 6m being the most active (IC50 = 12.96 µM for ABTS and 27.48 µM for α-glucosidase), outperforming the positive controls Trolox and acarbose. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate the binding interactions.

papers.title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides.
papers.abstract: Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI - a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed a
papers.summary: Pepti-DrugPhAI is a multimodal AI tool that predicts pharmacokinetic properties and toxicity for peptide drug candidates, addressing a major bottleneck in peptide therapeutic development. It combines multiple data modalities to evaluate functional PK and toxicity across a broad range of peptide compounds, aiming to reduce late-stage failures in preclinical and clinical trials.

papers.title: ML-QSAR and Fragment Selectivity for the Identification of Fourth-Generation EGFRL858R/T790M/C797S Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to establish an integrative workflow that couples QSAR modeling based on ML-QSAR, fragment-level selectivity analysis, large-library virtual screening, and MD simulations to identify fourth-generation inhibitors of the EGFRL858R/T790M/C797S mutant. Independent XGBoost models were trained on curated ChEMBL bioactivity data for mutant and wild-type EGFR, yielding strong predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.74-0.81; RMSE = 0.53-0.56) together with interpretable SHAP feature attributions. Fragment analysis highlighted structural motifs that were subsequently used to screen the ZINC databas
papers.summary: The authors built an integrated computational pipeline combining machine-learning QSAR models (XGBoost with SHAP interpretability) trained on ChEMBL data for mutant versus wild-type EGFR, fragment-level selectivity analysis, large-library virtual screening of ZINC, and MD simulations to prioritize fourth-generation EGFR inhibitors targeting the L858R/T790M/C797S mutant. The models achieved good predictive accuracy (R² 0.74–0.81) and identified structural motifs and candidate compounds with potential mutant selectivity. This is a computational drug-discovery study; experimental validation of the proposed hits is not reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Drug Design for Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming: A Critical Review.
papers.abstract: How can cellular interactions in solid tumors guide molecular interventions against immune suppression? This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) connects immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) states to testable molecular hypotheses. We distinguish observational artificial intelligence (AI) predictions from molecular intervention hypotheses and examine the experimental evidence required to evaluate them. We reviewed patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology using literature identified through 15
papers.summary: This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) can be used to identify and test molecular interventions that reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in solid tumors. It distinguishes observational AI predictions from actionable molecular hypotheses and outlines the experimental evidence needed to validate them, drawing on patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, simulation, and pharmacology.

papers.title: Virtual Screening-Derived Computational Lead Candidates for MAO-B Inhibition in Parkinson's Disease: Pathway-Informed Docking, Molecular Dynamics, DFT and ADMET Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) is a clinically validated target in Parkinson's disease (PD), but docking rank alone is insufficient to establish a CNS-directed inhibitor. We integrated MAOB-related pathway context, domain-resolved structural annotation, GNINA virtual screening, predicted blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeation, molecular dynamics (MD), density functional theory (DFT) and ADMET assessment to nominate hypothesis-stage computational candidates. A pharmacophore-derived input collection 2870 entries was subjected to virtual screening; a curated BBB-positive, favorable Vina/CNN-affinity s
papers.summary: This study integrates pathway context, GNINA virtual screening, blood-brain barrier prediction, molecular dynamics, DFT, and ADMET analysis to nominate computational lead candidates for MAO-B inhibition in Parkinson's disease. Starting from a 2870-compound library, the authors filter for BBB-positive compounds with favorable docking and CNN affinity scores, then validate top hits through MD and quantum chemical calculations. The work is hypothesis-generating and requires experimental validation before any therapeutic relevance can be claimed.

papers.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.
papers.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine
papers.summary: This review surveys computational approaches for simulating how PCSK9 variants behave structurally and dynamically, with the goal of informing therapeutic design against hypercholesterolemia. It highlights that clinical translation has focused on the rigid catalytic domain that binds LDLR, while the flexible C-terminal cysteine-rich domain remains underexploited as a target. The paper argues that emerging simulation methods can help bridge this gap for precision-medicine applications.

papers.title: Discovery of Two Potential and Novel Toll-like Receptor 7 Antagonists via Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulation and In Vitro Biological Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an important pattern recognition receptor. It mainly participates in the recognition of single-stranded RNA and is closely related to various disease processes. In humans, the enormous potential of TLR7 antagonists in reducing inflammation and alleviating autoimmune damage has been identified. Similar effects have also been observed in livestock and poultry. Therefore, using porcine TLR7 as the target, we combined virtual screening with a heterologous reporter gene assay to identify potential ligands, aiming to provide a research basis for the development of immu
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and dynamics simulations to virtually screen compounds against porcine Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), then validated hits with an in vitro reporter gene assay. Two novel TLR7 antagonists were identified, offering starting points for developing immunomodulatory drugs for inflammatory and autoimmune conditions in livestock and potentially humans.

papers.title: GPCRVS in the detection of target-selective molecular scaffolds based on deep learning and gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: High drug selectivity minimizes unintended interactions that cause adverse effects, decreases drug potency, and are failure-prone factors in many clinical trials due to a poor balance between drug efficacy and toxicity. Sharing similar structural folds and modes of activation, G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) may represent difficult drug targets in terms of optimization of pharmacodynamic profiles towards drug target selectivity. Here, we describe GPCRVS, a web service for GPCR virtual screening, designed to detect selective drug-like compounds. GPCRVS combines machine learning for ligand-ba
papers.summary: GPCRVS is a new web service for virtual screening of drug-like compounds against G protein-coupled receptors, combining deep learning and gradient boosting to identify target-selective ligands. It aims to help optimize drug selectivity for GPCRs, which share similar structures and are challenging targets for selective drug design.

papers.title: From AI-Generated Sequences to Therapeutic Peptide Candidates: A Disease-First Perspective on Computational Design, Developability, and Application.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides bridge the gap between small-molecule drugs and biologics, offering high target selectivity and broad opportunities for chemical and structural optimization. However, their clinical translation remains constrained by proteolytic instability, limited bioavailability, delivery barriers, safety concerns, and manufacturing challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) expands the generation and prioritization of peptide hypotheses through language models, target-conditioned design, structure-aware modeling, and multi-objective optimization. Experimental testing of disease-relevant
papers.summary: This review examines how AI methods—including language models, target-conditioned generative design, structure-aware modeling, and multi-objective optimization—are being used to generate and prioritize therapeutic peptide candidates. It frames the field from a disease-first perspective, emphasizing that clinical translation of peptides is limited by proteolytic instability, poor bioavailability, delivery barriers, safety, and manufacturing challenges, and that computational design must account for these developability constraints alongside activity.

papers.title: AI-driven transformation of GPCR research: from structural biology to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate complex pathophysiological networks and represent a critical class of drug targets, but their structural determination and ligand screening are constrained by dependence on homology templates, static conformations, and a bias toward known ligands. Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming GPCR structural biology and pharmacology by overcoming these bottlenecks. The methodologies encompass high-precision static structure prediction, dynamic conformational ensemble modeling, ultra-large-scale virtual screening, de novo ligand design, allos
papers.summary: This review describes how artificial intelligence is transforming G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) research, moving beyond template-based structural biology and static conformations toward dynamic ensemble modeling, ultra-large-scale virtual screening, and de novo ligand design. The authors argue these AI methods can overcome the bias toward known ligands and enable precision medicine approaches targeting GPCRs.

papers.title: Identification of potential natural PPARγ agonists via graph neural networks and integrated computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus has become a prevalent metabolic disease worldwide. Current synthetic PPARγ (Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ)agonists are associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need to explore natural compounds with potential PPARγ agonistic activity. PPARγ is a vital therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. To facilitate the discovery of natural PPARγ agonists, this study integrated graph neural network (GNN) prediction, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, in vitro activity assessment, and molecular dynamics simulations for multistage virtual screening. Three
papers.summary: This study combines graph neural network prediction, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, in vitro assays, and molecular dynamics simulations to screen natural compounds for PPARγ agonist activity, a target for type 2 diabetes. The multistage computational pipeline identified three candidate natural compounds with potential PPARγ agonistic activity, offering alternatives to synthetic agonists that carry adverse effects.

papers.title: A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization.
papers.abstract: AI-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) combines molecular modeling with machine learning to support lead identification and candidate prioritization. Conventional molecular descriptors principally encode static chemical structures, leaving frequency-domain behavior as an additional source of molecular information. We therefore developed the terahertz fusion descriptor (THz-FD), a feature-fusion framework that integrates terahertz (THz) frequency-domain features for Na+/K+-ATPase ligand classification and retrospective ranking. Extra Trees (ET), Random Forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) c
papers.summary: The authors developed THz-FD, a machine-learning framework that fuses conventional molecular descriptors with terahertz frequency-domain spectral features to classify Na+/K+-ATPase ligands and prioritize drug candidates. They benchmarked Extra Trees, Random Forest, and SVM classifiers on this fused feature set, showing that adding frequency-domain information can improve ligand classification and retrospective ranking. The work suggests that spectral behavior in the THz range carries complementary molecular information beyond static structural descriptors.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with High-Throughput Biological Testing for Antimicrobial Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is eroding the effectiveness of existing antibiotics, while conventional discovery continues to yield few clinically useful chemical classes. This critical narrative review evaluates how artificial intelligence (AI) has been integrated with high-throughput screening (HTS) and prospective biological testing in antibacterial discovery. Graph-based and generative models have produced prospectively confirmed active compounds, pathogen-selective candidates and structures outside familiar antibacterial scaffolds. Where studies included suitable comparators, AI-guided selecti
papers.summary: This review examines how AI has been combined with high-throughput screening and prospective biological testing in antibacterial drug discovery. Graph-based and generative models have produced prospectively confirmed active compounds, including pathogen-selective candidates and structures outside familiar antibacterial scaffolds. The authors evaluate these integrations and note that AI-guided selection can improve hit-finding efficiency where suitable comparators exist.

papers.title: Navigating the Pharma 4.0 revolution: how AI-enabled applications and predictive modelling shaped pharmaceutical development in the post-pandemic era: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Pharma 4.0 is touted to make processes more efficient and resilient to unforeseen circumstances, boosting productivity, speed and accuracy of pharmaceutical systems. Besides operational stability, these technological implementations could potentially improve clinical outcomes. AI-enabled Pharma 4.0 applications and predictive modelling are utilised in pharmaceutical development for the discovery of new compounds that could potentially be used as drugs for COVID-19. This systematic review examined how contemporary Pharma 4.0 technologies have impacted pharmaceutical development in the post COVI
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how AI-enabled Pharma 4.0 applications and predictive modelling have influenced pharmaceutical development in the post-COVID era, with particular attention to compound discovery for COVID-19 drugs. The authors synthesize evidence on how these technologies improve process efficiency, resilience, and productivity, and discuss their potential to enhance clinical outcomes beyond operational stability.

papers.title: Subtractive Genomic Approach for Identification of Pathogen-Specific Essential Genes as Target and Drug Repurposing in Major Foodborne Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Foodborne diseases pose a substantial threat to global public health and economic stability, with bacterial contamination occurring at multiple stages of the food supply chain. The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among foodborne pathogens has further complicated the prevention and treatment of these infections, underscoring the urgent need for novel, pathogen-specific therapeutic targets. In this study, a comprehensive subtractive genomics approach was employed to systematically identify bacterial key genes (bKGs) as drug targets and to explore corresponding potential therape
papers.summary: This study applies a subtractive genomics pipeline to identify pathogen-specific essential genes in major foodborne bacteria, filtering out genes shared with the human host to find candidate drug targets. The authors then pair these targets with drug repurposing candidates, aiming to address antimicrobial resistance in foodborne pathogens. The work is a computational target-discovery exercise without experimental validation.

papers.title: Screening of DPP-4 inhibitory peptides derived from the skin of Takifugu bimaculatus and analysis of their inhibitory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: To address the growing global type 2 diabetes mellitus burden, dietary intervention via dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibition provides a viable approach for glycemic control. Takifugu bimaculatus skin hydrolysates exhibit favorable hypoglycemic efficacy; however, the core active components remain uncharacterized.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes DPP-4 inhibitory peptides derived from the skin of the pufferfish Takifugu bimaculatus, aiming to explain the hypoglycemic effects previously observed for its hydrolysates. The authors screen the peptides and analyze their inhibitory mechanisms, positioning them as potential dietary agents for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
papers.abstract: The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blin
papers.summary: This computational study screened nineteen phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against three fungal protein targets linked to major wheat diseases (Fusarium graminearum and Puccinia graminis). Using multitarget docking combined with toxicity-guided prioritisation, the authors identify candidate natural compounds with potential antifungal activity. The work is entirely in silico and provides hypotheses for further experimental validation rather than demonstrated efficacy.

papers.title: A knowledge graph-driven literature-based discovery framework for drug repurposing in aplastic anaemia.
papers.abstract: Aplastic anaemia is a haematological disorder characterized by immune-mediated destruction of haematopoietic stem cells and bone marrow failure. Although immunosuppressive therapies are currently used, their lack of target specificity underscores the need for systematic approaches to identify precise therapeutic targets and explore drug repurposing opportunities.
papers.summary: The authors present a knowledge graph-based literature discovery framework aimed at identifying drug repurposing candidates for aplastic anaemia, a rare immune-mediated bone marrow failure disorder. By integrating literature-derived relationships into a graph, the approach systematically surfaces potential therapeutic targets and existing drugs that could be redirected to this disease. The work is a methodological application in a narrow clinical niche rather than a validated therapeutic finding.

papers.title: Immediate early response 3 promotes airway epithelial inflammation and represents a therapeutic target in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airway inflammation, yet clinically useful biomarkers and mechanistically validated therapeutic targets remain limited. Here, we aimed to identify and functionally validate smoke-responsive regulators of airway epithelial inflammation in COPD and establish an interpretable prediction framework by integrating population-based clinical data, multi-omics analyses, genetic causal inference, and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study identifies the gene IER3 as a smoke-responsive driver of airway epithelial inflammation in COPD, using an integrated approach combining population clinical data, multi-omics, genetic causal inference, and experimental validation. The authors propose IER3 as both a potential biomarker and a therapeutic target, and build an interpretable prediction framework for COPD.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, then structurally characterizes these interactions. The work suggests a mechanistic basis for the reported anticancer activity of these polyphenols in LUAD, though the findings are based on in silico prediction rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Investigating the Protective Role of Folic Acid in Fluoride-Induced Neurotoxicity: An Integrative Computational and In Vivo Study.
papers.abstract: Excessive fluoride exposure has been associated with neurotoxicity, including cognitive deficits and an increased risk of dementia. SIRT1, a key regulator of oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, is downregulated in fluoride-induced neurotoxicity. This study aimed to identify a potential nutraceutical compound that modulates SIRT1 and explore its effects in a rat model of fluoride-induced neurotoxicity.
papers.summary: This study used computational screening to identify folic acid as a potential modulator of SIRT1, a protein downregulated in fluoride-induced neurotoxicity, and then tested it in a rat model. The in vivo experiments reportedly showed that folic acid mitigated fluoride-induced neurotoxic effects, suggesting a protective nutraceutical role. The work integrates docking-based prediction with animal validation to propose a dietary intervention.

papers.title: AI-enabled drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease: from computational nomination to pharmacological proof.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the scale and speed of drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Transcriptomic signature matching, network-based systems pharmacology, real-world data pharmacoepidemiology and multi-omics machine learning have generated hundreds of candidate drugs, while repurposed agents account for 35% (56 of 158) of drugs and 42% (15 of 36) of Phase 3 agents in the 2026 AD pipeline. Clinical translation, however, remains unproven. Randomised trials of GLP-1 receptor agonists illustrate the gap between prioritisation and therapeutic proof: semaglutide did not sl
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI methods—transcriptomic signature matching, network pharmacology, real-world pharmacoepidemiology, and multi-omics machine learning—have generated hundreds of candidate repurposed drugs for Alzheimer's disease, with repurposed agents now comprising 35% of drugs and 42% of Phase 3 agents in the 2026 AD pipeline. However, the authors emphasize that computational nomination has not translated into clinical proof, citing the failure of semaglutide in randomized trials as an illustration of the gap between prioritization and therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of Coumarin-Triazole Derivatives Targeting the Conserved QGDNQ Motif of Chandipura RdRp.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV) is a recently discovered neurotropic virus associated with severe encephalitis in children and for which there is currently no specific antiviral treatment. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is an attractive antiviral target because of its essential role in viral RNA synthesis and the presence of conserved catalytic motifs required for polymerase function. In this study, a structure-based computational approach was employed to investigate coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors targeting the conserved QGDNQ motif-containing region of CHPV RdRp.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structure-based methods to identify coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of the Chandipura virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, targeting its conserved QGDNQ catalytic motif. The work is purely computational (docking-based), with no experimental validation reported, so the compounds remain hypothetical candidates for a virus that currently lacks approved antivirals.
